summary:
Sud is a region of Italy and stands under the Italian national framework. No regional statute, court ruling or administrative measure specific to Sud addressing gender identity or sexual orientation was identified in this inventory, so the assessment rests on documented incidents within the region.

ILGA-Europe's annual country review for Italy, published in February 2025, records a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence against LGBTI people in 2024, with incidents reported almost monthly. One such incident fell within this region: in March 2025 a young man was assaulted by attackers on a scooter in Scampia, a neighbourhood of Naples.

On 13 October 2025 a 63-year-old man was arrested in Torre Annunziata, in the province of Naples, after making stabbing threats against a young LGBTQIA+ activist; Il Gazzettino described it as a grave homophobic episode in the Naples area.

On detention, no dedicated transgender prison facility exists in Italy. A 2010 announcement that Pozzale, near Florence in Tuscany, would become one of the world's first prisons for transgender inmates was never realised; as of 2013 the facility had not been created, and trans detainees remain within the ordinary men's and women's prison circuit, including in this region.
tangentialFactors:
The incidents documented in Sud form part of a national pattern ILGA-Europe describes as increasing in both number and geographic spread during 2024, with reports arriving almost monthly across Italy rather than concentrating in any single area.

The Pozzale proposal announced in January 2010 was Italy's only documented special-unit initiative for trans prisoners; its non-realisation by 2013 means trans detainees nationwide, including in Sud, are housed in ordinary facilities with no dedicated unit anywhere in the country.
localsOnly:
Residents of Sud live under the national Italian legal framework, and no region-specific protective statute or administrative measure addressing gender identity or sexual orientation was identified in this inventory for the region.

Regional anti-discrimination statutes exist in several other Italian regions (Tuscany 2004, Liguria 2009, Marche 2010, Sicily 2015, Piedmont 2016, Umbria 2017, Emilia-Romagna 2019, Campania 2020, Apulia 2024), but no equivalent statute for Sud appears in this inventory.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Sud has any pending regional anti-discrimination bill or administrative guidance on gender identity is unresolved in this inventory; the absence of a statute here is a research finding, not a confirmed legislative decision.

The current status of the Pozzale trans-prison proposal after 2013 is unresolved; no later reporting appears in this inventory, and the record does not establish whether the plan was formally cancelled or simply lapsed.

The February 2025 ILGA-Europe review's characterisation of a rise in 2024 violence rests on reported incidents; the inventory does not provide a denominator or reporting-rate context for that increase.
